verification: On an existing independent Rust-exported slate, the new Python native-reply replay exactly reproduced all 65 checked candidate scores. complete_games.qualification: These are fresh diagnostic games for an already rejected hybrid, not an Elo rating or a promotion gate. Native teacher is the direct opponent; policy-induced states differ across agents.

sampled_native_reply_ranking.sampling: Hybrid root turns with round modulo8 equal to zero
sampled_native_reply_ranking.descriptive_loss_overlap: Only four of 15 lost seat-zero games and four of 21 lost seat-one games had a strict native-reply regret at a sampled hybrid root turn. The 1-in-8 round sampling cannot rule out errors on other turns.

interpretation: A decisive seat-one-only candidate-ranking failure does not appear on these sampled hybrid-visited positions: each seat has five strict native-reply-regret positions, and the paired independent-map seat comparison is inconclusive. The hybrid's lower game win count and sampled score-ranking errors must not be causally equated. Earlier teacher-rollin positions had 22 strict-regret positions in154 and 19 affected maps in32, but those are different maps and state distributions, not a paired comparison. Sparse sampling leaves much of the actual game trajectory unobserved.
decision: Keep the hybrid rejected and unrated. Do not tune on seed6360000, run reserved hybrid confirmation seed6357000 or final promotion seed6300000, or deploy it. If studying search-error credit further, predeclare a fresh full-turn-coverage or exact counterfactual outcome experiment rather than extrapolating from this 1-in-8 sample.
